item.content:encoded:
AI agents exploit medical software flaw to access university server

Category: AI

Amazon said attackers used autonomous AI agents to find and exploit a previously unknown flaw in MONAI Label, open-source medical-imaging software, during a September campaign against universities in East Asia. The agents went from mapping the software’s interface to writing files on a server in about 11 minutes; in a later session, they used the flaw to obtain root access. Amazon linked the activity with moderate confidence to a China-linked actor, but did not identify a group or establish government involvement [18][20]. Separately, a wave of U.S. outages from Nov. 12 to 17 affected Microsoft services, banking, Apple apps, aviation and an NSA network. Officials cited technical failures and patching problems, not evidence of a coordinated cyberattack; some vulnerabilities behind the repairs had been found with AI [13][14][42]. MONAI Label maintainers merged a source-code fix on Oct. 19 but had not yet issued a patched release [18].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

The patch needs to go instantly from being available to being patched in production, because it’s being exploited in the wild. So that’s going to create its instability.

— Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella (The Next Web)

Key Points

  • Separate cyberattack: Criminals compromised the legitimate marketing platform Optimizely and planted malicious code on more than 170 websites, including the BBC, CNN and Zoom, to steal payment details and redirect about US$7,000 [49].
  • Prompt exposure: Dragos said a five-month test using nearly two million canary-laced prompts found evidence of data exposure at three AI providers and prompt access by inference-marketplace resellers [15].
  • Policy review: A U.S. Government Accountability Office assessment published Nov. 20 set out 16 policy options, including standardized testing and stronger safeguards for AI model lifecycles [9].
  • Patch volume: The number of software vulnerabilities recorded in 2026 passed 100,000, compared with about 25,000 in 2022, according to Wired [13].
  • Exploit gap: The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency listed 300 vulnerabilities as exploited in 2026, while VulnCheck counted 1,500. Both figures are far below the more than 100,000 vulnerabilities found overall [13].
  • VPN exposure: TeamT5 chief executive Tsai Song-ting said attacks on web servers and VPN devices have increased and warned that a compromised VPN can give attackers direct access to a company’s internal network [1].
  • Cybersecurity hiring: Microsoft issued more than 1,400 product security patches in October—about 10 times its historic baseline—while US cybersecurity hiring has lagged overall hiring, according to LinkedIn data reviewed by The New York Times [34].
  • Hidden flaw: Cybersecurity researcher Paulos Yibelo used AI tools to find a Ghostscript flaw that allowed an uploaded file with a specially crafted font to trigger malicious code. The software developer and affected companies issued fixes after he notified them [41].
  • Patch race: Bridgewater said the average time from vulnerability disclosure to exploitation fell from about a month to 11 days, while the number of recorded flaws under active exploitation surged [7].
  • Open-source burden: A significant share of internet infrastructure relies on open-source software maintained by small volunteer teams, leaving some widely used components with limited resources for security fixes [23][7].

Perspectives

Former U.S. cybersecurity agency director Chris Krebs: Microsoft, IBM and Google are using frontier AI models to find bugs before attackers do, Krebs said. He argued that defenders should keep using AI to identify and patch those bugs [42].

Sources: PBS

TeamT5 cybersecurity: Chief executive Tsai Song-ting argued that companies cannot rely on fully automated AI defense because defenders bear the consequences of mistaken decisions. He recommended prioritizing critical assets and temporarily taking a system offline when a severe flaw cannot be fixed quickly [1].

Sources: Central News Agency

OpenRouter: The AI router said it had removed three providers and revoked Zero Data Retention eligibility for 125 endpoints after Dragos’s findings. It said the research did not show a breach of OpenRouter itself [17].

Sources: Rescana

Satya Nadella, Microsoft chief executive: Nadella warned that much critical infrastructure runs firmware that cannot be patched, citing chillers, heating and cooling systems, and internet-connected transport networks [37].

Sources: The Next Web

Christopher Krebs, former director of the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency: Krebs warned that AI-enabled offensive frameworks are scanning company networks continuously for vulnerabilities, eroding the time defenders once had to respond [42].

Sources: PBS NewsHour

Mahmoud Elkhodr, senior lecturer in information and communication technologies at CQUniversity Australia: Elkhodr calls for governments to require critical-service operators to test how long they can keep core functions running without their usual global technology providers [49].

Sources: Scroll.in

Timeline

  • 8 September 2026: Cairn agents began a roughly 48-hour university-targeting campaign [19]
  • 19 October 2026: MONAI Label maintainers merged a source-code fix for the flaw [18]
  • 20 November 2026: The U.S. Government Accountability Office published its AI cybersecurity assessment [9]
  • 12 November 2026: Microsoft services went down for users in more than 70 countries and territories [45].
  • 13 November 2026: The FAA ordered a nationwide ground stop after communications equipment failed [54].
  • 16 November 2026: Bank customers reported transaction and account-access problems at major US institutions [45][54].
  • 17 November 2026: Apple services and an NSA internal network experienced separate disruptions [45].

Technical Details

  • Microsoft gateway failures: A gateway-server patch deployed in July contained a latent defect. A shift of Teams traffic to a shared gateway coincided with reduced system capacity, and automated traffic rerouting added load as servers failed [54].
  • MONAI Label path traversal: The vulnerable upload function appended a user-supplied file identifier to a storage path without checking that the resolved file remained inside the approved folder; the default server configuration also lacked authentication [18].
  • AI inference routing: An inference router may forward prompts through several providers, each able to see the full request and response; Dragos said privacy settings such as Zero Data Retention were not consistently honored across the chain [15].
  • Root access chain: In a later session, agents planted a Python startup file and triggered a training process that loaded it, creating a reverse shell with the privileges of the server account [18][19].
  • Disclosure-to-exploitation window: Bridgewater’s analysis says the average time from vulnerability disclosure to exploitation has fallen from about a month to 11 days, increasing the risk that attackers exploit a flaw before downstream users install its patch [7].

Industry Impact

  • Service disruption fallout: The Microsoft outage halted routine procedures such as releasing detainees from US jails and accessing some patient records at UK hospitals [14].
  • Medical-imaging research: MONAI Label is a server used by research teams to annotate medical scans and train imaging models; it is separate from the broader MONAI framework [18].
  • AI service providers: Dragos said stolen canary credentials were used in attempts to access its controlled test systems and AWS accounts, showing how exposed prompt data can put connected cloud resources at risk [15].

Historical Background

In 1991, a typo in new code from telephone company DSC Communications helped take down millions of phone lines over several months. The company had skipped its customary 13-week testing period because it considered the upgrades minor [23].

Q&A

Q: What signs should operators check for if a MONAI Label server was reachable?

A: Administrators should look for unexpected Python startup files and unusual training jobs, which could indicate the file-write flaw was used to launch code [18].

Q: Did Amazon confirm a second university was compromised?

A: No. Amazon said agents later received a tunnel into a second university network running the same software, but it had not confirmed that network was compromised [18].

Action Items

  • Restrict exposed MONAI Label servers: Block untrusted network access, enable authentication, run the service with a limited account and verify that any source build includes the fix before treating it as patched [18].
  • Review AI-provider prompt handling: Check router and provider incident notices, rotate credentials previously included in prompts, and ask vendors where prompts are routed and retained [17].

item.content:encoded:
Anthropic AI proof clears formal checks, but human review remains

Category: AI

An AI-assisted proof of the Riemann hypothesis by Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge has passed formal checks by two groups: the Lean Focused Research Organization, which advances the Lean proof system, and the Mathlib Initiative, which supports its mathematics library. The groups said on Nov. 21 they had “full confidence” in the proof Alpöge developed with Anthropic’s Claude model [19][9][16]. The checks establish that the formalized code proves the Riemann hypothesis as defined in Mathlib, but do not provide mathematicians with a readable account of the argument. The proof consists of a Lean library of about 17 million lines, and Alpöge has said the argument is too large to present as a conventional paper at this stage [16][1][18]. The certification does not constitute formal acceptance of the problem as solved. The Clay Mathematics Institute requires a solution to appear in a peer-reviewed journal and withstand at least two years of scrutiny before it can consider awarding its $1 million prize [33][9].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

I imagine the digestion process will take some time, though in this case at least we have a human author to communicate with to assist with this task.

— Terence Tao, mathematician (BBC)

Key Points

  • Broader claim: Alpöge also said the approach proves the generalized Riemann hypothesis, which extends the conjecture to related L-functions [48][33][41].
  • Prize conditions: The Clay Mathematics Institute selected the hypothesis as one of seven Millennium Prize Problems and offers $1 million for an accepted solution [33][48].
  • Broader claim: Alpöge said his method also extends to the generalized Riemann hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions; that claim is separate from the certification of the Riemann-hypothesis proof [2][20].
  • Human alternative: Stanford professor Ravi Vakil said postdoctoral researcher Alessandro Masullo had submitted an independent, AI-free draft concerning the generalized Riemann hypothesis; the manuscript still needs substantial revision and review [41][42].
  • Historical reach: Efforts to prove the hypothesis helped develop techniques used in algebraic geometry, probability theory, quantum physics and dynamical systems [48].
  • Model access: Alpöge said he worked with a non-public version of Claude for about six weeks, limiting outside researchers’ ability to reproduce the discovery process with the same model [8][19].
  • Parallel claim: Stanford professor Ravi Vakil said a postdoctoral researcher in his department had independently submitted a proof of the hypothesis [33].
  • Audit results: MIT mathematician Andrew Sutherland reported that all 175,187 Lean modules compiled without errors; an axiom audit found that the five headline theorems relied only on Lean’s three standard axioms [9][16].
  • Independent checkers: Lean’s kernel and third-party checkers accepted the formal proof export, while the tools comparator and con-leche separately confirmed that the encoded theorem matches Mathlib’s Riemann-hypothesis statement [16][1].

Perspectives

Ngô Bảo Châu, Fields Medal-winning mathematician: He argued that fears that mathematical research is ending are misplaced, and described AI as a tool that could expand mathematical work and make it more accessible [12].

Sources: 36Kr

James Maynard, Oxford number theorist: He said he suspects the proof will be correct, while cautioning that checking it will take time and understanding why it works will require substantial effort [29].

Sources: Nacionale

Andrew Sutherland, MIT mathematician: He said he was both nervous and excited about the future, noting that researchers may need years to understand how the proof works and where its methods can be applied [35].

Sources: The Hindu BusinessLine

Brian Conrey, a leading specialist on the Riemann hypothesis, said he had not yet seen a manuscript and had asked for a copy. He also thought there might be simpler ways to present the proof [33].

Sources: TheJournal.ie

Timeline

  • August 2026: Anthropic said Claude improved a bound but had not proved the hypothesis [11]
  • September 2026: OpenAI claimed an AI-assisted solution to the Navier-Stokes problem [43]
  • 20 November 2026: Alpöge published his Claude-assisted claim and linked Lean proof files [19]
  • 21 November 2026: Lean and Mathlib groups announced confidence in the formal proof [19]

  • Export safeguards: The proof was checked as an inert export, beyond the reach of code in the Lean source; con-leche and con-ron also have formal proofs, relative to set theory, that they cannot accept a false proof [16].
  • Statement matching: Reviewers used comparator and con-leche to check that the code’s theorem matches the Riemann-hypothesis statement already defined in Mathlib [1].
  • Mathlib statement: The Riemann-hypothesis statement already existed in Mathlib and had been vetted by experts; a challenge file isolated it and imported only Mathlib for comparison [16].
  • Kernel verification: Lean’s kernel replay found no rejected modules, while independently developed checkers also accepted the exported proof [1].

UN summit in Barbados to focus on AI safety capacity gaps

Category: AI

The United Nations’ Special Summit on AI Safety is due to open Monday, Nov. 23, in Bridgetown, Barbados, with national preparedness, international risk management and wider access to the benefits of artificial intelligence (AI) on its agenda [3][2]. Finland’s Minister of Transport and Communications Lulu Ranne will represent the country in place of President Alexander Stubb [2]. The meeting will bring together government, technology, scientific and civil-society representatives. Military uses of AI are excluded, and organizers expect calls to action and pledges rather than a negotiated agreement [3][1]. UN Secretary-General António Guterres and Barbados Prime Minister Mia Mottley are co-hosting the hybrid summit [3].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

AI is one of the most significant technological breakthroughs in human history. AI is a good servant but a bad master, so it is vital that humans remain in control.

— Lulu Ranne, Finland’s Minister of Transport and Communications (Valtioneuvosto)

Key Points

  • Response gap: Amandeep Singh Gill, UN special envoy for digital and emerging technologies, cited World Development Report 2026 figures showing 500 incident-response teams in high-income countries and six in low-income countries [3].
  • Framework proposal: Gill said the proposed multilateral risk-management framework is intended to help countries build national AI safety infrastructure [3].
  • Expected attendance: About 150 people are expected, including a senior U.S. diplomat and Chinese experts [3].

Perspectives

Amandeep Singh Gill, UN special envoy for digital and emerging technologies: National AI preparedness cannot be measured only by a country’s ability to build AI systems, Gill argued; countries also need the capacity to test models developed elsewhere.

Sources: Superpower Daily

Historical Background

In September 2026, Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre issued a call on frontier AI models; by mid-November, 36 leaders from 34 countries and the European Commission had signed it [2][1].

Critics cited by NPR say demands for shareholder returns could weigh on decisions such as delaying a risky model for additional safety testing. Anthropic’s prospectus warns that safeguards may prove inadequate or be circumvented, and says the company could ultimately lose control of its models [16]. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has said safety and public benefit are built into the company’s mission [16]. Anthropic has made large, long-term infrastructure commitments and uses chips from Nvidia, AMD, Google and Amazon for model training and inference, according to reporting on its filings and supplier relationships [2][26]. Its Long-Term Benefit Trust can appoint four of seven directors, and the company markets its safety approach to enterprise and government customers [16][11].

Critics cited by NPR say demands for shareholder returns could weigh on decisions such as delaying a risky model for additional safety testing. Anthropic’s prospectus warns that safeguards may prove inadequate or be circumvented, and says the company could ultimately lose control of its models [16]. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has said safety and public benefit are built into the company’s mission [16]. Anthropic has made large, long-term infrastructure commitments and uses chips from Nvidia, AMD, Google and Amazon for model training and inference, according to reporting on its filings and supplier relationships [2][26]. Its Long-Term Benefit Trust can appoint four of seven directors, and the company markets its safety approach to enterprise and government customers [16][11].

Primary Source: View original article

“There is a gigantic difference between how AI will go if we pay little attention to safety versus how it will go if we are obsessed with safety.”

— Dario Amodei, Anthropic chief executive (NPR)

Key Points

  • Supplier investment: Seven semiconductor and technology suppliers bought non-voting shares in Anthropic’s private placement, giving them a financial stake in a major customer [2].
  • Customer stakes: Anthropic markets its safety approach to enterprise and government customers concerned with security, data handling and predictable model behavior [11].
  • Index buying: Intropic estimates funds tracking stock indexes could buy as much as 30% of Anthropic’s shares by year-end, though those purchases are not guaranteed [40].
  • Enterprise demand: Anthropic reported more than 11,900 customers generating at least $100,000 in revenue over the preceding 12 months as of September, compared with about 1,500 in 2025; its revenue run rate reached $81 billion by Oct. 31 [58].
  • Safety governance: Anthropic is a public benefit corporation; its Long-Term Benefit Trust can appoint four of seven directors, while the founders control appointments to the other three [16].
  • Bank fees: The deal generated $550 million in fees for Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley and 20 other banks, according to Bloomberg data cited by The Business Times [58].
  • Share supply: About 300 million additional Anthropic shares are due to become tradable on Dec. 15, which some investors said could add pressure to the stock [34].
  • Options trading: Options on Anthropic shares were expected to start trading the following week, giving investors another way to bet on or hedge against price swings [40].
  • Trust dissolution: Legal experts cited by NPR said the founders and shareholders with voting rights could dissolve the trust, potentially allowing them to override its influence during a major safety dispute [16].

Perspectives

Jonathan Golub, chief equity strategist at Seaport Research Partners, said the AI-stock selloff looked excessive and demand for computing power remained strong. He identified financing hundreds of billions of dollars in new infrastructure as a challenge [35].

Sources: Bloomberg

Avery Marquez, Renaissance Capital investment-strategy director: Marquez said the valuation debate and uncertainty about an AI bubble have become more pronounced because Anthropic is a newly listed stock, and that investors need time for price discovery [6].

Sources: CNBC

Jonathan Golub, Seaport Research Partners chief equity strategist: Golub argued that the AI-driven market selloff looked excessive because demand for computing power remained strong and semiconductor earnings expectations were rising, while warning that markets must still finance hundreds of billions of dollars in infrastructure [14].

Sources: Bloomberg

Raphael Thuin, Tikehau Capital head of capital-markets strategies: Thuin said his firm prefers diversified businesses for AI exposure and would wait for post-IPO price volatility to subside before considering a position in Anthropic [58].

Sources: The Business Times

Timeline

  • 2020: Dario and Daniela Amodei left OpenAI and founded Anthropic with five colleagues [54]
  • 19 November 2026: Shares opened at $111.50, above the $83 offer price, and closed at $97.17 [24]
  • 20 November 2026: Shares closed at $88.91, down 8.5% from Thursday but about 7% above the offer price [13]
  • 18 November 2026: Anthropic priced shares at $83, above its marketed range [60]
  • 19 November 2026: Shares began trading on Nasdaq and closed 17% higher [21][59]
  • 20 November 2026: Shares fell as technology stocks sold off broadly [59][6]

Technical Details

  • Direct procurement: Under its “Anthropic Direct” strategy, Anthropic contracts separately for accelerators, CPUs, memory and networking equipment, and leases data-center space and operations, rather than bundling them through public-cloud providers [2].

Industry Impact

  • Venture capital exits: Anthropic’s listing delivered large paper gains to early backers: at the IPO price, Menlo Ventures and Lightspeed Venture Partners each held stakes worth about $25 billion, CNBC reported [21].
  • Public-market benchmark: Anthropic is the first frontier AI model maker to list, so its disclosures could give investors a direct reference point for evaluating AI developers rather than relying only on chipmakers and data-center suppliers [58][59].
  • Enterprise software: Anthropic’s efforts to sell Claude for coding and other corporate tasks depend on expanding beyond coding tools and chatbots, which account for roughly three-quarters of corporate spending on generative-AI application services [4].

Historical Background

The listing followed a prolonged slowdown in venture-backed IPOs: technology companies raised $73 billion in 2021, compared with $39 billion over the following four years, according to data from University of Florida emeritus professor Jay Ritter cited by CNBC [21]. The number of technology companies going public fell from 126 in 2021 to 34 in 2025 [21].

Q&A

Q: How can the safety trust be removed?

A: The Long-Term Benefit Trust can be dissolved only with approval from all seven co-founders and a majority vote among shareholders with voting rights [16].

Q: How quickly are Anthropic’s computing costs rising?

A: Anthropic spent nearly $9 billion on computing capacity and infrastructure in the first half of 2026, then reported another $5 billion in computing expenses in the third quarter [3].

Q: Was there significant investor interest during Anthropic’s debut despite the later retreat?

A: Retail investors traded about $772 million of Anthropic shares on Thursday, the most for an IPO debut since Vanda Research began tracking the data in 2012 [40].

Developers publish manifesto urging human review of AI-generated work

Category: AI

Software developers and attendees at the AIE Code Summit published a “No AI Slop” manifesto on Nov. 22, urging people to take responsibility for AI-assisted work and review outputs according to the stakes. The signatories warn that AI agents can produce more code and documentation than a person can assess, while unchecked errors can be copied into later work [2]. A study of local open-weight models found that agents often identified the vulnerable code and formed a correct hypothesis but failed to produce a working input that would trigger the vulnerability [9]. Separately, Together AI said an AI coding agent committed a repository credential that enabled an unauthorized party to download stored prompt samples. The company said it was continuing to review potentially exposed customer data [15].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

AI cannot replace human judgement, it can only amplify our judgement (or lack thereof).

— AIE Code Summit 2026 speakers and attendees (GitHub)

Key Points

  • Trace failures: A case study of 100 support-agent traces recorded 12 failures, including seven cases in which the agent asked for details instead of calling a tool and two involving misapplied policy rules [6].
  • Security changes: Together AI said it made zero data retention the default for new accounts, added credential checks to pull requests and changed development rules for AI coding agents [15].
  • Model testing: Researchers tested 12 local model configurations on 10 vulnerability-reproduction tasks. Every configuration handled most of the six easier tasks, while the four harder tasks required the 27-billion-parameter model [9].
  • Review standard: The manifesto argues that success should be measured by what users receive and how it helps them, rather than code volume, merged pull requests or the number of agents running [2].

Perspectives

Together AI: The company said it is investigating what customer information may have been exposed and will notify affected customers directly; it advised customers handling sensitive prompts to enable zero data retention [15].

Sources: Together AI

Technical Details

  • Vulnerability reproduction: The study tested whether agents could turn a vulnerability description into an input that crashes a vulnerable software build, a task researchers describe as closer to test generation than code comprehension [9].
  • Trace grading: EvalSift Lite, a trace-grading tool, validates JSONL agent traces, applies deterministic code checks and generates a Markdown or HTML failure report. It runs without an API key or external dependencies [6].

Industry Impact

  • Software development: The manifesto calls for teams to improve systems and guardrails when a mistake recurs, and to rely on automated checks for problems that linters, type checkers or similar tools can catch [2].
  • AI services security: The stored prompt samples came from requests to the MiniMax M3, GLM-5.2 and Kimi K2.6 models, primarily on June 24, July 4, July 8 and July 14, 2026 [15].

Scientific Significance

  • Performance detail: Quantization did not change which tasks models solved in matched comparisons, though it affected speed; the mixture-of-experts model achieved the same scores in less wall-clock time [9].
  • Limits of evidence: The study used three runs per task under a single testing harness, so its results describe that benchmark rather than all software-development work [9].

item.content:encoded:
FBI probes crime-database breach as hackers target USDA payment system

Category: Technology

The FBI is investigating an apparent intrusion into its National Crime Information Center (NCIC), a database used by federal, state and local law enforcement, while the U.S. Department of Agriculture separately told employees that hackers targeted a system used to pay farmers [4][14][2]. Officials have not established whether the incidents are connected or who was responsible [2][8]. The scope of the FBI incident remains unclear: it is not known whether attackers accessed sensitive NCIC records or stole information. The FBI has not publicly confirmed the incident or responded to requests for comment [3][4]. A former FBI official warned that inaccurate NCIC records could affect officers’ decisions and public safety [14]. Former USDA officials told NBC News that access to the payment system could provide a route to more sensitive food-safety data and research on animal-borne illnesses [2][5]. President Donald Trump called the reported FBI breach “not good,” then suggested it might reveal information about voter fraud [4][6]. ABC News reported that NCIC would not hold information on the Russia and Ukraine investigations Trump also invoked [24]. The FBI and USDA incidents are being described as cyberattacks, distinct from recent service outages that officials attributed to routine system upgrades and vulnerability fixes [2][4].

  • Cyber director: The White House fired National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross during the week of the reported breaches, as criticism mounted over outages affecting key services [2][17].

A separate 2023 incident involved a computer system used by the FBI’s New York field office in child sexual exploitation investigations, CNN previously reported [14].

item.content:encoded:
GTA 6 launches at 30 fps as leak fuels unofficial PC port efforts

Category: Technology

Rockstar Games released Grand Theft Auto VI on Nov. 19 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, targeting 30 frames per second on every console to preserve the density of its environments and crowds. Rockstar technology production director Marc Chambers said the PlayStation 5 Pro’s stronger graphics processor improves effects such as ray-traced shadows, but its CPU cannot handle the game’s complex simulation at 60 fps [16]. Rockstar has not announced a PC release date [23]. An Xbox Quick Resume glitch can remove the frame-rate cap on Series X. Players report 45 to 100 fps, but the glitch also speeds up gameplay and causes inconsistent performance in crowded areas [9][7]. Reports on Series S performance conflict: Digital Foundry testing cited by IOL found frame rates in the low 20s during heavy explosions, while early hands-on reviews described smooth play [14][6]. Some PS5 players also report crashes that block story progress; Rockstar has not confirmed a fix [26]. An anonymous leaker known as Cyberleek says a 209 GB Xbox build is available but has withheld the executable, promising to release it Nov. 23. The files have not been independently confirmed as genuine [21]. A separate volunteer project, Leonida, says its recompilation work cannot yet boot the game and its developers need the executable to begin that step [19].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

This community will have it emulated inside a week, running far past 30fps.

— Cyberleek (Mashable)

Key Points

  • Player engagement: On launch day, 61% of active U.S. PlayStation 5 users and 56% of global Xbox users played GTA VI. Players averaged 513 minutes on PlayStation and 494 on Xbox, Circana adviser Mat Piscatella said [1].
  • Console network: PlayStation Network experienced scattered outages before launch but recovered quickly, and preload downloads had no widespread failures. The eventual launch of GTA Online will pose a larger network test, Push Square said [11].
  • Crash reports: Some Xbox Series X players also reported crashes, and Rockstar support directed players with console error codes to Sony or Microsoft for help [26].
  • Crypto condition: Decrypt reported that Cyberleek offered to release the executable early if its CYBERLEEK token reached a market value of $15 million. The token’s market value was around $1.3 million at the time [21].
  • PC groundwork: Leonida says it has translated 26,503 Xbox graphics shaders into SPIR-V, but its graphics layer still lacks pipelines, draw calls and a swapchain [19].

Perspectives

Xbox Series S players: Mashable’s reviewer urged players who cannot upgrade not to let console comparisons spoil the experience, arguing the game remains immersive on Series S despite unknown graphical trade-offs [6].

Sources: Mashable

Leonida developers: The project says it is built from users’ own readable game files and does not decrypt them or bypass protection [19].

Sources: GitHub

Timeline

  • 19 November 2026: Grand Theft Auto VI launched on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S [9][26]
  • 21 November 2026: Players publicized a Quick Resume glitch that removes the 30 fps cap [7][9]
  • 23 November 2026: Cyberleek’s promised release date for the withheld Xbox executable [12][21]

Technical Details

  • Frame-generation processing: Veyra and NeuralScreen can apply upscaling and frame generation to captured console video, but the console still renders gameplay at 30 fps; added processing can increase input latency [17].
  • Wave64 shader support: Leonida says 21,545 shaders use wave64; translation is exact on 64-wide subgroups, while some vertex, pixel and geometry operations remain approximate on 32-wide subgroups [19].
  • Supported graphics operations: Leonida’s Vulkan-backed layer can handle queues, command lists, fences, resource creation, barriers, clears, uploads and copies; the repository says these operations have been checked on one GPU [19].

item.content:encoded:
Rockstar says GTA VI generated record $3.79 billion on launch day

Category: Technology

Rockstar Games said Grand Theft Auto VI generated an estimated $3.79 billion in worldwide retail sales on its first day, Nov. 19, calling it the biggest entertainment launch in history. The new entry in the crime-game series sold 32.5 million copies before release and is available only for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S [10][21][2]. The $3.79 billion represents estimated customer spending at retail, not the amount Rockstar or parent company Take-Two Interactive received after retailers and platform operators took their shares [4]. The figure is nearly five times the roughly $800 million estimated for predecessor Grand Theft Auto V’s first 24 hours in 2013; GTA V later sold nearly 235 million copies [3][12]. Neither a PC edition nor the online multiplayer component has a confirmed release date. Analysts at Wells Fargo forecast sales of 65 million copies by Take-Two’s fiscal year-end in March 2027, while TD Cowen analyst Doug Creutz said the scale and timing of future recurring spending in GTA Online matter more to the company’s stock than unit sales alone [12][6].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world and we couldn’t be more excited to share this moment with you

— Sam Houser, president and founder of Rockstar Games (Associated Press, published by Channel 3000)

Key Points

  • Review divide: Metacritic showed a 99/100 average from about 150 professional reviews but a 5.5/10 user score from nearly 45,000 ratings, with some players criticizing bugs, originality and the lack of a 60-frame-per-second mode [12].
  • Player engagement: Circana data cited by TechSpot found 61% of active U.S. PlayStation 5 owners and 56% of active Xbox owners worldwide played the game on launch day [5].
  • Audience beyond consoles: Stream Charts counted more than 132 million hours of GTA VI viewing across Twitch, YouTube and Kick on launch day [4].
  • Launch-day absences also rose: BrightHR reported a 56% increase in UK sickness absence versus the previous Thursday, while provisional data suggested about 35,000 more secondary school pupils missed school [5].

Perspectives

Take-Two Interactive CEO Strauss Zelnick: Earlier this month, Zelnick said the company was not ready to declare success before the launch because it avoids claiming success before it occurs [6].

Sources: The Indian Express

U.S. police departments: Several departments warned players not to imitate the game’s car thefts, reckless driving and violence; Atlanta police wrote, “GTA is not a real place, but Atlanta is!” [21].

Sources: The Guardian

Timeline

  • 2013: Grand Theft Auto V recorded about $800 million in first-day sales [3]
  • 2022: A hack exposed stolen gameplay footage from the game [22][9]
  • 2025: Rockstar moved the planned release from fall 2025 [2]
  • 26 May 2026: The announced May release date was later postponed [2]
  • 19 November 2026: Grand Theft Auto VI launched on PlayStation and Xbox consoles [10][21]

Technical Details

  • Independent measurement: Sensor Tower estimated roughly 24.6 million units and $2.36 billion in revenue, while Rockstar reported 32.5 million pre-release units and $3.79 billion in launch-day retail sales. The figures use different methodologies and time windows [10][4].

Industry Impact

  • Telecoms: Preloads pushed Virgin Media O2’s evening traffic 9.4% above its previous record, while GTA VI accounted for as much as 24% of Comcast traffic at peak; BT and EE also reported new home-broadband peaks [1][5].

Historical Background

GTA VI was the first new mainline entry in the series in 13 years. Rockstar spent more than eight years developing it, with its production budget estimated at $1 billion to $1.5 billion [10][12].

Business Angle

  • An extended promotional trailer released in August helped drive a sixfold increase in pre-orders, according to Sensor Tower estimates [6].

item.content:encoded:
Signal details mobile screen-capture controls, including timed opt-outs

Category: Technology

Signal has detailed mobile controls designed to stop operating-system AI agents from reading chats displayed in its encrypted messaging app. The protections are available on iPhones running iOS 27 or later with Signal 8.37 or later, and on Android with Signal 8.35.1 or later [8]. They address the risk that agents can inspect a conversation after it has been decrypted for display, beyond Signal’s control [12][5]. On iPhone, users can turn off the protection or pause it for 10 minutes; on Android, Signal activates Screen security when it detects an assistant trying to read the screen [8][13]. Signal says these screen-capture measures do not block other routes to on-device data, and it cannot reliably provide the same protection on macOS [1][8].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

In order to gain access to information about you, these OS AI agents 'scan' the information that's on your screen.

— Meredith Whittaker, president of the Signal Foundation (The Hacker News)

Key Points

  • Developer requests: Signal wants Apple, Google and Microsoft to offer a documented opt-out covering screen reading, file access, notifications, APIs and other operating-system pathways [1][2].
  • Agent permissions: Meta’s Muse agent accessed Signal on Android through notification permissions and on a Mac through accessibility and screenshot tools, according to reported examples [1][7].
  • Android override: Signal says it will restore protection after 90 days if an Android user disables it through a Screen security prompt; disabling it directly in Privacy settings does not trigger reminders [8].

Perspectives

Signal: The company said it is discussing with Apple and Google how to make their systems work better with privacy-sensitive apps [2].

Sources: Coywolf

Meta: Meta said agents need to see and interact with users’ computers to act on their behalf, and that Muse accesses other apps only through permissions users explicitly grant [7].

Sources: The Economic Times

Timeline

  • 21 May 2025: Signal enabled default Windows 11 screen protection against Recall [8]
  • October 2026: Apple added an Excluded Apps option in iOS 27.2 [1]
  • 20 November 2026: Signal announced default mobile screen-capture protections [2][8]

Technical Details

  • Android detection limits: Signal says differences among Android manufacturers make attempted screen capture difficult to detect consistently, so its protection activates only when it recognizes an AI assistant reading the display [8][12].

Action Items

  • Exclude Signal from Siri access on a Mac: Open System Settings, go to Siri, and add Signal to “Excluded Apps,” as Signal recommends for macOS [4].

item.content:encoded:
Mexico captures FBI-wanted cartel leader in raid that leaves 11 dead

Category: World

Mexican forces captured Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as “El Chapo Isidro,” in Guasave, Sinaloa, on Friday night, Nov. 20, in an operation that left four soldiers and seven suspected cartel gunmen dead, Mexico’s Defense Ministry said. Meza Flores, who was flown to Mexico City, is on the FBI’s Ten Most Wanted list. U.S. authorities accuse him of trafficking drugs and illegally possessing firearms [1][4][2]. The raid triggered armed clashes, vehicle burnings and roadblocks across parts of Sinaloa. Videos showed baseball fans fleeing gunfire in Guasave, while local authorities urged residents to stay indoors. The government said U.S. intelligence helped locate Meza Flores; The New York Times reported that U.S. and Mexican authorities had shared intelligence for weeks [11][46][16]. Meza Flores was allied with Los Mayos, a faction fighting for control of the Sinaloa Cartel after its co-founder Ismael “El Mayo” Zambada was taken into U.S. custody in 2024. President Donald Trump has pressed Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum to intensify action against cartels, including by linking trade policy to security progress. Meza Flores is now in the custody of Mexican prosecutors, and the United States has sought his extradition [18][6][5].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

We’re working with her on the cartels because the cartels are running Mexico. I told her that. And we can’t let the cartels run Mexico. They’re our neighbour

— President Donald Trump (Financial Times)

Key Points

  • Other detainees: Authorities said eight people were arrested overall: Meza Flores and two senior associates were taken to Mexico City, while five others remained in Sinaloa [4][10].
  • Weapons seized: Security Minister Omar García Harfuch said authorities recovered a.50-caliber rifle, a grenade launcher and hand grenades, as well as drugs and cash [20][10].
  • Baseball suspended: The Mexican Pacific League canceled the remaining weekend games after gunfire disrupted the Guasave match [46][48].
  • Reward offer: The U.S. State Department had offered up to $5 million for information leading to Meza Flores’ arrest [7][4].
  • Additional allegations: When the FBI added Meza Flores to its most-wanted list in 2025, it also cited alleged kidnapping, extortion and torture; these remain allegations [5][31].

Perspectives

Mexican Security Minister Omar García Harfuch: He called the arrests an important step toward pacifying Sinaloa and said federal security forces would remain deployed to protect residents [28][43].

Sources: La Vanguardia

Security experts: Experts cited by the Financial Times questioned whether removing cartel leaders can curb violence without stronger policing and efforts to address political corruption and money laundering [6].

Sources: Financial Times

Timeline

  • 2012: U.S. authorities first indicted Meza Flores on drug-trafficking charges [4]
  • 2013: U.S. Treasury sanctioned Meza Flores under the Kingpin Act [4]
  • 2024: Zambada’s U.S. custody preceded fighting between Sinaloa factions [18]
  • February 2025: The FBI added Meza Flores to its Ten Most Wanted list [29]
  • 20 November 2026: Mexican forces captured Meza Flores in Guasave after a firefight [4][42]
  • 21 November 2026: Authorities transferred Meza Flores to Mexico City prosecutors [15][10]

Historical Background

The U.S. Treasury imposed sanctions on Meza Flores under the Kingpin Act in 2013, freezing his assets [4].

Humanitarian Impact

Authorities reported no civilian deaths in the raid, despite the armed clashes and panic in the surrounding area [12][46].

International Reactions

  • 🇺🇸 United States: U.S. Ambassador to Mexico Ronald Johnson credited strategic intelligence sharing with helping make the capture possible [18][20].
  • 🇺🇸 U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration: The agency welcomed the arrest as a significant victory against a violent criminal network [30][34].

item.content:encoded:
COP31 final draft omits fossil fuels, leaving deal at risk

Category: World

COP31 negotiators in Antalya were still seeking consensus on Sunday after a proposed final agreement again omitted an explicit commitment to move away from fossil fuels, the central dispute at the U.N. climate summit [12][32][10]. The draft refers indirectly to a 2023 agreement on the transition, recognizes that the world is on course to exceed the 1.5-degree Celsius warming threshold, and backs a goal of raising electricity’s share of global final energy use to 35% by 2035. It also calls for faster development of carbon-removal technologies [12][2]. The text followed overnight consultations among summit co-presidents Turkey and Australia and delegations from nearly 200 countries. It does not restore the proposed $120 billion annual adaptation-finance target that developing countries had sought, and it sets no requirement that new power for the electricity goal come from renewables [38][4]. Countries still needed to approve the proposed text. The scheduled session was delayed, and reports did not confirm that a final agreement had been adopted [4][10]. Departing delegations could also reduce attendance below the two-thirds quorum needed for a decision [5].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

It’s better to have no deal than to have a bad deal.

— Wopke Hoekstra, European Union climate commissioner (Financial Times)

Key Points

  • Global stocktake: The 2028 global stocktake is intended to assess countries’ climate efforts and shape subsequent emissions-cutting plans [1].
  • Import savings: The International Energy Agency estimated that electrification could save developing countries about $100 billion in fossil-fuel imports by 2035 [1].
  • Carbon capture: The draft retains an aspirational aim to scale carbon capture, use and storage toward one gigatonne by 2035, despite opposition from delegates and campaigners [38][10].
  • Finance dispute: The latest draft replaces the $120 billion target with further discussions on a pathway to triple adaptation finance, while leaving countries’ contributions voluntary [38].
  • Carbon capture dispute: The latest text scaled back its commitments to carbon capture, use and storage, which may be enough to ease the EU’s concerns [31].
  • Science timetable: Countries also disagree over when the next Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change assessment reports should appear: several want them before the 2028 global stocktake, while India and Saudi Arabia favor 2029 [14][36].
  • Roadmap gap: The draft also omits a Brazil-led global roadmap for transitioning away from fossil fuels, a demand of several countries and campaign groups [38].
  • Electricity claims: A document sent anonymously to some delegations from poorer countries portrayed the proposed electrification goal as binding national quotas, although the UN described it as a global target, with countries free to choose their own pathways [1].

Perspectives

COP31 President Murat Kurum, Turkey’s environment minister, said he believed the new text could win agreement and urged delegates to weigh it carefully, saying people outside the negotiating hall were already experiencing climate impacts [2][4].

Sources: BBC News

Tuvalu climate minister Maina Talia called an explicit fossil-fuel commitment a red line for Tuvalu, saying it addressed the root cause of climate change [5][31].

Sources: Financial Times

Ghana’s environment minister, Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings, said, “We didn’t come here to beg,” as developing countries called for climate finance to help them adapt [25][42].

Sources: The National

Australia: Climate Change and Energy Minister Chris Bowen argued that the summit should focus on implementing the shift to clean energy rather than requiring fossil-fuel language in the final text [30].

Sources: BBC News

Tuvalu: Climate Minister Maina Talia described a reference to fossil fuels as a red line for the low-lying island nation, calling them the root cause of the crisis [31].

Sources: BBC News

Timeline

  • 2015: Paris Agreement set the goal of limiting warming to 1.5C [31].
  • 2023: IPCC published its most recent full climate assessment [1].
  • October 2026: IPCC plenary was put on hold as countries disputed its next assessment schedule [1].
  • 22 November 2026: Third COP31 draft acknowledged the world is on track to miss 1.5C [31].
  • 2028: Global stocktake is scheduled to review countries’ climate efforts [1].

Technical Details

  • CCUS mechanism: The technology captures emissions as they are released and stores them underground [31].
  • Carbon capture record: Critics of the draft’s carbon-capture language point to its high cost and limited record of reducing emissions, and warn that reliance on it could prolong fossil-fuel use [2][26].
  • Power-mix caveat: The proposed 35% electricity-share objective does not require the added electricity to come from renewable sources rather than coal or gas [2].

Scientific Significance

  • Assessment timing: If the next IPCC report arrives after the 2028 global stocktake, that review would lack the panel’s latest synthesis of climate science [1].

Historical Background

At COP28 in Dubai in 2023, governments agreed to transition away from fossil fuels, but did not set targets or deadlines for doing so [8][11]. At COP30 in Brazil last year, the hosts pledged to develop a global roadmap for phasing them out [8].

Q&A

Q: What would happen if delegates cannot approve the text?

A: If consensus fails, negotiations could be suspended until next year; such a breakdown has occurred only once since COP meetings began in 1995 [4].

France protests enter sixth weekend as turnout falls and clashes flare

Category: World

Protesters in France demonstrated over living costs and public services for a sixth consecutive Saturday on Nov. 21, with the Interior Ministry counting 82,500 participants nationwide and organizers estimating 150,000. Both figures were down from the previous weekend and far below the 800,000 organizers said had joined the first large march on Oct. 17 [4][11][10]. Students, unions, left-wing groups and Yellow Vest activists marched over living costs, housing, education and public services. Protesters also opposed a new law expanding legal protections for police who use firearms [4][36]. Most marches were peaceful, but police used tear gas to disperse unauthorized gatherings in Lyon, and clashes and fires were reported in several cities. The Interior Ministry reported 144 arrests by 6 p.m. An AFP tally cited by French media counted at least 31 people seriously injured by security forces since the protests began; authorities have issued no official injury total [11][15][4][9]. Youth- and worker-led rallies also took place in Portugal and Spain [8][11]. French unions have called another public-sector strike and demonstrations for Dec. 1, demanding higher public-sector pay and renewed wage negotiations [20][21].

In a number of countries, young people are going through the same thing, namely precarity. You have to choose between having a roof over your head, getting medical care, and being able to eat your fill.

— Manon Moret, general secretary of the Unef students’ union (Le Monde)

Key Points

  • Paris turnout: Police counted 21,500 participants in the capital, while organizers estimated 45,000 [15][11].
  • Police law: The Senate passed the law 205-110. It presumes officers acted lawfully when using firearms, though evidence can rebut that presumption. The left says it will challenge the measure before the Constitutional Council [36][2].
  • Housing pressure: In Portugal, average annual earnings in 2025 were 37% below the EU average, while house prices had more than doubled since 2017 [11][7].
  • Care-home protest: In Madrid, demonstrators demanded accountability and compensation for 7,291 care-home deaths during the first COVID-19 wave in 2020 and called for publicly run care homes [11].

Perspectives

French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez: After passage of the police firearms law, Nunez urged regional authorities to be “particularly vigilant regarding the groups most hostile to law enforcement” [4].

Sources: Le Monde

Gabriel Amard, France Unbowed lawmaker: He criticized the new law, arguing that it shifts the presumption in police shooting cases toward treating the shooting as lawful [36].

Sources: O Globo

French trade unions CFDT, CGT and Unsa: Public-sector unions want an increase in the salary base rate, but the government has ruled out raising it in 2027 [20].

Sources: Anadolu Agency

Timeline

  • September 2026: High-school students launched protests over learning conditions [4][15]
  • 17 October 2026: First large march drew 800,000 by organizers’ count [4][11]
  • 20 November 2026: Parliament adopted the police firearms law criticized by demonstrators [10][36]
  • 21 November 2026: Sixth consecutive Saturday of protests brought 82,500 by ministry count [4][15]
  • 1 December 2026: Unions scheduled another public-sector strike and mobilization [20][21]

Historical Background

The Yellow Vest movement began in 2018 in protest against rising fuel taxes and later broadened to address living costs and social inequality [11][4]. The current protest wave began in mid-September with high-school students demanding better learning conditions, before unions and other groups joined [4][15].

item.content:encoded:
Finnish officials suspect Ukraine struck Russian cargo ship in Gulf of Finland

Category: World

The Russian cargo ship Sparta II caught fire after two drones struck it in international waters in the Gulf of Finland on Saturday, then drifted into Finnish waters. Finnish armed forces spokesperson Aki-Mauri Huhtinen said Ukraine was likely responsible, though Kyiv had not commented [2][7]. The 16 crew members left the ship for a nearby Russian vessel, while Finnish authorities led the rescue operation as the fire continued to burn [2][6]. The ship was bound for Kaliningrad and has links to Oboronlogistika, a Russian logistics company that serves the Defence Ministry. Finland’s Border Guard said the ship’s cargo was unconfirmed and could include military material. The ship is under U.S. sanctions [2][6]. Finnish authorities also suspected that a Russian helicopter briefly entered Finnish airspace hours after the strike, possibly during rescue or surveillance operations [8][10]. Finland imposed temporary air and maritime restrictions in the eastern Gulf of Finland, informed its allies and began coordinating the response. Russian vessels could tow the damaged ship back [2][7][23]. Finland’s defence minister said the Border Guard would investigate the attack with other authorities [7].

Primary Source: View original article

The war is spilling over into our neighbouring areas. Finnish authorities are handling the situation in the Gulf of Finland, where a drone strike has hit a Russian merchant vessel. Ukraine has the right to fight against the aggressor.

— Petteri Orpo, Prime Minister of Finland (ABC News (Australia))

Key Points

  • Drone barrage: Leningrad Region Governor Aleksandr Drozdenko said Russian air defences downed 80 drones over the region overnight, though the figure has not been independently verified [21][23].
  • Ust-Luga damage: Drone strikes also damaged Novatek’s oil-product terminal and petroleum-product infrastructure at Ust-Luga, Ukraine’s Security Service said [23].
  • Diesel exports: Baltic ports’ role in fuel trade grew after an October agreement allowed Russia to partially resume diesel exports; the first tanker carrying diesel left Primorsk that month [23].
  • Ship dimensions: The Russian-flagged Sparta II is 121 metres long and left St. Petersburg for Kaliningrad on Friday, according to shipping data cited by Reuters [6][12].

Perspectives

Alexei Besprozvannykh, Governor of Kaliningrad: He said the incident posed no threat to supplies reaching the Russian exclave [7].

Sources: BBC News

Kristen Michal, Prime Minister of Estonia: He said the attack showed the consequences of resisting Russian aggression had reached the Baltic Sea and that Estonia would continue supporting Ukraine [15].

Sources: TimesLIVE

Aleksandr Drozdenko, Governor of Leningrad Region: He initially said the crew did not need evacuation and planned to resume the voyage after completing necessary work. Finnish authorities later reported that the crew had left the ship [10][7].

Sources: Agence France-Presse

Timeline

  • 2022: Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine [2][10]
  • 11 November 2026: A drone strike hit Russian corvette Naro-Fominsk in the Gulf [23]
  • 21 November 2026: Drones struck the Sparta II in international waters [7][2]

Industry Impact

  • Baltic shipping: The Gulf of Finland connects St. Petersburg to open Baltic waters; the wider Baltic Sea carries about 15% of global freight, and attacks have raised risks to routes used by cargo ships and oil tankers [23].
  • Russian grain exports: Baltic ports handled 65.3% of Russia’s seaborne grain exports in October, with Ust-Luga the country’s largest grain export port that month at 684,000 tons [23].

Historical Background

Russia’s invasion prompted Finland to end decades of military non-alignment and join NATO in 2023; Sweden followed in 2024 [10][2].

International Reactions

  • 🇸🇪 Sweden: Swedish combat aircraft operating under Finnish command helped safeguard Finland’s and NATO’s territorial integrity after the incident, Sweden’s defence minister said [6].
  • 🇪🇪 Estonia: Estonia sent a navy vessel to assist with firefighting and pollution response [2][15].

Q&A

Q: Could Finnish authorities inspect the ship’s cargo?

A: Finnish authorities said they had no plans to bring the ship to Finland. If it were brought into the country, officials could inspect its cargo if they determined there were grounds to do so [26].

item.content:encoded:
Iran strikes Bahrain as Hormuz tanker attacks deepen Gulf standoff

Category: World

Bahrain said an Iranian attack caused a fire at a civilian industrial facility on Saturday, Nov. 21, causing material damage but no injuries. Iran’s Revolutionary Guard Corps said it had instead targeted U.S. positions at the Al-Riffa and Awali bases with missiles and drones, claiming it hit two Patriot air-defense radars. Bahrain reported intercepting several incoming attacks, and the U.S. military had not confirmed damage to its bases [1][4][2][5]. Projectiles also struck two tankers transiting the Strait of Hormuz, according to the U.K. Maritime Trade Operations center. Iran’s army said another vessel caught fire after hitting a mine in a restricted area, while the U.S. military said it had cleared mines from the main routes. The strait carried about one-fifth of global oil before the war. Iran has sought to restrict shipping through it, while the United States has imposed a counter-blockade of Iranian ports [3][12][2]. Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said a Qatari delegation held two hours of mediation talks in Tehran on Friday. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Iran would not discuss reopening the strait until its demands—including an end to the war and U.S. blockade—were met. Iran’s electricity company said rolling power cuts would begin Sunday, Nov. 22, citing fuel supply conditions [1][4][13].

Our position is clear: as long as Iran's demands are not met, the discussion on the Strait of Hormuz and its opening is pointless.

— Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi (Al-Monitor)

Key Points

  • Tanker damage: The maritime agency said one tanker was hit in the stern and another in its engine room; no casualties were reported in either incident [2][12].
  • Oil movement: U.S. Central Command said last month it had helped Gulf states export 1.5 billion barrels through Hormuz since the summer [3][1].
  • Nuclear red line: Araghchi said Iran would not allow its enriched-uranium stockpiles to leave the country, a central dispute in U.S.-Iran relations [3][13].
  • Regional warning: Bahrain’s air-defense interceptions caused shrapnel damage, and authorities issued public shelter alerts before and after an all-clear [2][5].
  • Power cuts: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said strikes on energy infrastructure had worsened domestic energy problems ahead of winter [1][3].

Perspectives

Bahrain’s Foreign Ministry: It called on the U.N. Security Council to take firm measures to make Iran implement Resolution 2817, which condemns attacks on Gulf states and demands a halt to hostilities and maritime interference.

Sources: Al Jazeera

Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps: The force said its attack responded to alleged U.S. drone incursions and an attack on a radar installation on Iran’s Hengam Island, and warned that further violations of Iranian airspace would draw a decisive response.

Sources: Al Jazeera

Sources: Euronews

Sources: Asharq Al-Awsat

  • 28 February 2026: The United States and Israel launched strikes on Iran, beginning the war [2].

  • August 2026: Washington announced an economic campaign to curb Iran’s trade and financial flows [3].
  • 21 November 2026: Bahrain reported an industrial-site fire as tankers were struck in Hormuz [1][3].

  • 🇯🇴 Jordan: Jordan condemned the strike as a violation of Bahrain’s sovereignty and international law, calling it a dangerous escalation [4].

  • 🇶🇦🇩🇪 Qatar and Germany: Their joint statement condemned attacks and threats against commercial vessels and called for compliance with U.N. Security Council Resolution 2817 [22].

Q&A

Q: What is Iran demanding before it will discuss reopening Hormuz?

A: Tehran has said it wants the war ended on all fronts, Iranian assets unfrozen, oil sanctions lifted and the U.S. counter-blockade of Iranian ports ended [4][2].

Canada says military ties with U.S. continue as Ottawa diversifies

Category: Canada

Canadian Defence Minister David McGuinty said he had seen no change in military cooperation with the United States despite a reported Pentagon directive limiting some contacts. Mike Rounds said the guidance mainly requires U.S. military officials to obtain permission to attend Canadian think-tank events or social functions and does not affect operations [10][4]. item.content:encoded:
B.C. premier merges mining into resource ministry, removes climate portfolio

Category: Canada

British Columbia Premier Lorne Doerkson unveiled a smaller cabinet on Nov. 20, combining mining with energy and petroleum resources and removing climate change from the names of key ministries [1][3]. The cabinet has 18 ministers, plus Doerkson and six ministers of state; the former New Democratic government had 23 ministers. Doerkson’s Conservative government also says it will repeal the Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act (DRIPA), which provides for joint project decisions with First Nations [1][2]. The new cabinet includes rookie MLAs in major portfolios. Finance Minister Peter Milobar says the government will commission an independent review of provincial finances; the latest forecast cited by The Canadian Press put the deficit at nearly $14 billion [3][4]. Doerkson said the legislature will not sit this fall, though his government is considering orders-in-council. The Narwhal reported that MLAs are unlikely to return before February. The first cabinet meeting is scheduled for next week [1][3].

Primary Source: View original article

I am committed to repealing DRIPA because it hasn’t worked

— Lorne Doerkson, British Columbia premier (The Narwhal)

Key Points

  • Health portfolio: Health Minister Ryan Peterson will oversee a ministry with about $40 billion in expenses; Doerkson said he selected him for his business background [3][4].
  • Resource projects: B.C. has 41 major projects, including 16 in critical minerals and mining; the Conservatives have pledged fixed permitting timelines and a “one project, one review” approach [1].
  • LNG target: The party’s platform promises to double liquefied natural gas production by 2032 and triple it by 2035; LNG Canada in Kitimat is the province’s only operating export facility [1].
  • Campaign spending: The Conservatives’ plan proposed adding $1.4 billion in annual operating spending while reducing the deficit within three years [3][4].

Perspectives

Montreal police make first arrests in force misconduct probe

Category: Canada

The first criminal arrests in a Montreal police misconduct investigation have prompted civil-rights advocates to call for accountability and wider scrutiny. One said the case could set a precedent for holding officers responsible [1][9]. Allegations involving a second station, downtown Station 21, include mistreatment of unhoused people and a claim that an officer urinated on someone while on duty [4][9]. item.content:encoded:
European-Japanese BepiColombo enters Mercury orbit ahead of two-probe science mission

Category: Science

BepiColombo, a joint mission of the European Space Agency and Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency, entered orbit around Mercury on Nov. 21, completing an eight-year journey and becoming the second mission to orbit the planet [4][2][13]. The two orbiters remain attached; they are scheduled to separate on Dec. 9–10 and take up different polar orbits, with science operations due to begin in April 2027 [1][2]. The mission will use the European Mercury Planetary Orbiter and Japan’s Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter, called Mio, to study Mercury from separate vantage points. Their instruments are designed to examine the planet’s surface and interior, its magnetic field and the thin gas envelope around it, including how the magnetic field interacts with the solar wind [2][4]. Controllers in Germany confirmed the spacecraft’s capture several hours after a series of braking thruster firings, with the spacecraft about 152 million kilometers away [4]. A propulsion-system problem delayed BepiColombo’s arrival from December 2025. Its nominal science mission is planned to last one Earth year, with an extension through 2029 [2].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

What makes this mission really unique is that for the first time in space exploration, we are bringing two spacecraft to the vicinity of the planet, and we are going to put them in orbit around this mysterious body.

— Santa Martinez, European Space Agency mission manager for BepiColombo (Eos)

Key Points

  • Orbital paths: Mio is headed for a highly elliptical polar orbit, while the European orbiter will use a less elliptical polar orbit [1].
  • Long route: The spacecraft made one Earth, two Venus and six Mercury flybys to shed speed; the looping trajectory covered more than 10 billion kilometers [4][1].
  • Energy challenge: Reaching Mercury is harder than reaching Pluto because a spacecraft must shed enough momentum to match Mercury’s path around the Sun [2].
  • Mission cost: The joint mission is valued at about $2 billion, or 1.7 billion euros [4][2].

Perspectives

Daniel Schmid, research-group leader at the Austrian Academy of Sciences’ Space Research Institute, said measurements of the strength and direction of Mercury’s magnetic field could help explain why the planet has a global field [6].

Sources: ORF

Timeline

  • October 2018: BepiColombo launched from French Guiana on its Mercury-bound mission [4][13].
  • 2024: Thruster problems prompted a trajectory change and delayed Mercury arrival [2][13].
  • 3 September 2026: The transfer module separated from the still-connected science orbiters [1][7].
  • 21 November 2026: BepiColombo entered Mercury orbit after braking thruster firings [4][1].
  • 9 December 2026: The European and Japanese orbiters are scheduled to separate [2][1].
  • 10 March 2027: The European orbiter is scheduled to reach its nominal science orbit [1][12].
  • April 2027: The mission’s science operations are scheduled to begin [2][13].

Technical Details

  • Gravity and radio measurements: The European orbiter’s altimeter will map surface elevation, while its accelerometer, gravitometer and radio-science experiment will help map Mercury’s gravity and determine the size of its core [2].
  • Magnetic-field observations: Mio will map the magnetosphere, magnetic field and plasma environment. Researchers aim to investigate why Mercury’s field is offset from the planet’s center and how it varies [2].
  • Thermal management: The spacecraft use metallic-coated insulating films and multilayer insulation to manage temperature extremes; plans also call for one orbiter to spin 15 times per minute to reduce overheating [6][14].

Scientific Significance

  • Polar scans will search for water ice, while comparisons with MESSENGER observations may reveal changes on Mercury since that mission visited about a decade earlier [7].

Historical Background

NASA’s Mariner 10 flew past Mercury in the 1970s. NASA’s MESSENGER was the only spacecraft to orbit the planet before BepiColombo, from 2011 until it ran out of fuel and struck the planet in 2015 [4][2].

item.content:encoded:
Ebola death toll in Congo exceeds 5,700 as response lags

Category: Science

An Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 11,700 confirmed cases and 5,700 deaths as of Nov. 19, making it the country’s largest and deadliest. Cases have also been reported in Uganda, Kenya and Nigeria [1][3]. The Bundibugyo strain is driving the outbreak, and no approved vaccine or targeted treatment is available for it. Health workers say early cases can be difficult to identify because initial symptoms resemble those of other illnesses [1][2]. Late detection, population movement and mistrust of response teams have hindered containment, while attacks on health workers and burial teams have further complicated the response [1][3]. On Nov. 17, health workers in Butembo, North Kivu, escalated a month-long strike over unpaid wages and bonuses, halting even minimum service at treatment centers [6].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

Coming early, before there are complications, gives patients more chances of survival

— Vivuya Kavira Mwenga, nurse at the Doctors Without Borders Ebola treatment center in Beni (EL PAÍS)

Did you know: The current outbreak crossed 10,000 confirmed cases in 163 days, 51 days faster than the 2014-16 West African epidemic [1].

Key Points

  • Treatment outcomes: Six Ebola treatment centers supported by ALIMA have received 1,243 patients, nearly 70% of whom recovered, according to Le Potentiel [5].
  • Children at risk: Children accounted for 28% of confirmed cases but 35% of deaths; by Nov. 4, 1,737 of the 2,959 people under 18 with confirmed infections had died [3].
  • Cases reach Europe: France confirmed a case in June in a doctor returning from a humanitarian mission in Congo; a British doctor who tested positive in Congo in November was flown to London for treatment and recovered [1].
  • Funding shortfall: International Rescue Committee response director Katie Thomas-Canfield said cuts in U.S., U.K. and German aid weakened surveillance and community relationships before the outbreak grew [1].

Perspectives

Doctors Without Borders (MSF): International president Dr. Javid Abdelmoneim said resources committed to the response were not effectively reaching patients, frontline staff and communities. He called the situation after six months unacceptable [3].

Sources: EL PAÍS

Julien Harneis, UN special coordinator for Ebola: Responding to MSF’s criticism, Harneis said teams could operate 80% of the time despite the area’s immense size [3].

Sources: EL PAÍS

Health workers in Butembo: They said negotiations were at an impasse after the provincial health coordinator failed to attend a meeting they had requested [6].

Sources: Libération

Timeline

  • February 2026: The outbreak is estimated to have begun in mid-to-late February [1]
  • May 2026: WHO detected the outbreak and declared it an emergency in mid-May [1]
  • September 2026: The number of affected health zones increased from 60 to at least 68 after Sept. 1 [1]
  • 17 November 2026: Butembo health workers halted minimum service as they escalated their strike [6]
  • 19 November 2026: Confirmed cases passed 11,700 and deaths exceeded 5,700 [1]

Historical Background

The 2014-16 West African Ebola epidemic caused 28,600 cases and 11,300 deaths [2]. The current epidemic is the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s 17th Ebola outbreak [3].

Humanitarian Impact

The U.N. reported 260 attacks on health workers in the outbreak’s first six months, and many deaths have occurred outside treatment centers [1][3].

Q&A

Q: How long could it take to bring the outbreak under control?

A: The U.N. has warned that ending the latest surge could take up to 12 months, if funding is available [2].

item.content:encoded:
Court halts Army plan to detonate five tons of lead azide in Iowa

Category: Science

A federal court temporarily halted the U.S. Army’s plan to detonate 68 drums of degraded lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant near Middletown after environmental groups challenged an emergency permit and raised concerns about lead dust spreading across Iowa and western Illinois [6][4][8]. The Army had rescheduled the blasts for Monday, Nov. 23, after objections from the public and elected officials; the court’s pause leaves it unclear whether they can proceed that day [5][6]. The Army says the material became more sensitive to shock and friction after liquid evaporated during prolonged storage, making transport hazardous and controlled detonation the safest immediate option. The plan calls for wetting the soil and using sand barriers to limit airborne particles, but the amount of lead likely to escape remains uncertain [2][9]. University of Iowa researchers and the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency planned to sample air and surfaces. The EPA was expected to respond to the lawsuit by Nov. 22, while the judge set no date for further action [4][6].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

The unprecedented aspect of it is that normally in the world of air pollution, we have some estimation of what’s called the emission factor, the emission strength. We know how many pounds per second will be distributed out into the air from a smokestack.

— Patrick O’Shaughnessy, University of Iowa professor of occupational and environmental health (Al Jazeera)

Key Points

  • Alternative disposal: The Army hired Georgia-based MuniRem Environmental to chemically neutralize the explosives, then canceled the contract. The company’s chief executive said the Army offered no explanation beyond citing its safety assessment [3][5].
  • Farm concerns: Some dairy farmers worried that cattle could ingest lead that settled on pasture grass. Most crops had already been harvested, reducing the potential for lead to settle on them [4].
  • Exposure testing: University of Iowa researchers planned to collect airborne dust as the plume passed and use gauzelike pads to sample settled material, with laboratory results expected about a week after detonation [4].
  • State response: Iowa Gov. Kim Reynolds activated the state Emergency Operations Center, while Cedar Rapids prepared to monitor drinking water drawn from the Mississippi River [5].

Perspectives

U.S. Army: Acting Army Secretary Adam Telle said the Army moved the operation to Monday as the latest possible moment before a forecast temperature drop that could further destabilize the material [5].

Sources: CNN via KRDO

Iowa Environmental Council and Sierra Club’s Iowa chapter: The groups asked a federal appeals court to overturn the emergency permit, arguing the public lacked meaningful advance notice, safeguards were inadequate and safer disposal options had not been sufficiently considered [2].

Sources: Al Jazeera

Illinois Department of Public Health: Director Sameer Vohra advised potentially affected Illinois residents to remain indoors with windows closed for 24 to 48 hours and wash hands and outdoor surfaces to reduce exposure [9].

Sources: NBC Chicago

Timeline

  • March 2026: Army surveillance found degraded lead azide in storage bunkers [5][9]
  • 15 October 2026: Army officials held a community meeting about possible detonation plans [5][9]
  • 13 November 2026: EPA approved emergency permit for controlled detonation [9][5]
  • 20 November 2026: Originally scheduled blast was postponed following public and official objections [6][2]
  • 21 November 2026: Federal judge paused the plan after environmental groups sued [6][4]
  • 22 November 2026: EPA was due to file its response in court [6]

Technical Details

  • Stockpile composition: The 68 barrels held about 9,700 pounds of lead azide, containing roughly 6,900 pounds of lead by chemical mass [2].
  • Blast effects: The Army warned that noise and ground vibrations from the detonation could cause localized window damage [6].
  • Forecast conditions: For the rescheduled Nov. 23 date, the preliminary forecast called for slower winds toward the south-southeast, potentially affecting a smaller area but bringing higher lead concentrations to those downwind [4].

Scientific Significance

  • Lead persistence: Lead cannot be destroyed by heat; experts said the blast could convert or disperse it into fine particles and compounds that settle into soil and on outdoor surfaces [2].
  • Model estimates: The Army's models predicted elevated airborne lead levels, but below the threshold at which the EPA would require protective actions [2].
  • Health vulnerability: Lead exposure can harm the brain and nervous system, and experts highlighted particular risks for young children and developing fetuses [4][2].

Historical Background

The material had been in storage for more than 20 years before its deterioration was discovered [5][9]. The emergency permit authorized detonation through Feb. 11, 2027, and required the Army to track potential air and dust dispersion and notify the public five days in advance [9][5].

Q&A

Q: What would happen if the court allows the operation to proceed?

A: Fort Madison officials said they had been told the detonation could happen Monday or Tuesday. If it did not take place that week, another date would need to be arranged with additional planning [5].

Q: What cleanup steps are recommended after the plume passes?

A: The Army recommended hosing down windowsills, cars and other horizontal surfaces where dust could collect, and washing outdoor toys and play areas. Washing moves lead from surfaces into soil rather than eliminating it [4].

Trump threatens tax on overseas AI data centers as chip curbs tighten

Category: Business

President Donald Trump threatened to impose a “tremendous tax” on U.S. companies that build artificial intelligence data centers abroad, saying he wants computing capacity concentrated in the United States to keep pace with China. He offered no details on how the tax would work and said he had not yet told his advisers about the proposal [12]. Separately, the Commerce Department issued new licensing requirements targeting Chinese access to advanced U.S. chips, including remote access through overseas servers [3][8]. U.S.-based infrastructure also delivers Chinese AI models to global customers. Some overseas data centers help companies comply with local data-storage rules and reduce transmission delays [3][12]. Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping are due to meet at the G20 summit in December; the countries’ trade truce is set to expire Jan. 10, 2027 [8].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

China can hit back, and they can hit back hard.

— Han Lin, China country director for The Asia Group (CNN)

Key Points

  • U.S. infrastructure concentration: Nvidia, Google, AMD and Amazon design nearly all deployed data-center AI chips, while Amazon, Microsoft and Google together control more than half of cloud services [3].
  • China’s alternatives: Huawei is developing an Atlas 950 SuperPoD designed to link as many as 8,192 Ascend chips; it demonstrated a 1,024-chip network in July [11].
  • Local opposition: U.S. communities have raised concerns about data centers’ electricity demand, utility bills and water use. A bill passed by the Senate would require large facilities to cover their own power costs; it still needs House approval [12].
  • Industrial policy: China’s 2026-2030 Five-Year Plan prioritizes technological self-reliance, advanced manufacturing and wider AI adoption [5].

Perspectives

President Donald Trump: He argued that U.S. companies should build data centers at home rather than overseas and suggested firms could negotiate with local communities over electricity costs, tax breaks and other benefits [12].

Sources: eToday

Kyle Chan, Brookings Institution: Chan said Chinese firms can draw on shared industrial expertise and supply networks, but government priorities for expanding capacity may conflict with companies’ commercial returns [5].

Sources: Firstpost

Timeline

  • March 2025: Amazon Web Services added DeepSeek-R1 to its Bedrock cloud platform [6]
  • July 2026: Huawei demonstrated a working network connecting 1,024 Ascend chips [11]
  • 20 November 2026: Trump threatened a large tax on firms building data centers abroad [12]

Historical Background

The United States introduced restrictions on exports of advanced semiconductors and chipmaking equipment to China in 2023, citing national security concerns [7]. In October 2025, President Trump and Xi Jinping agreed to reduce tariffs and roll back some export controls [1][8].

Business Angle

  • Moonshot AI reportedly requires companies with more than $20 million in annual sales that serve its Kimi K3 model to negotiate a license. It has sought 30% of Kimi K3 revenue from Microsoft, Amazon and Google [3].
  • Cloud hosting can offer enterprise buyers privacy, uptime and technical-support guarantees, while self-hosting makes a company’s own IT staff responsible for cybersecurity and maintenance [6].

International Reactions

  • 🇨🇳 China: China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs called the U.S. chip restrictions economic coercion, while the Ministry of Commerce warned it would respond if Washington persisted [8].

Q&A

Q: What leverage does China have in a dispute over chip access?

A: Analysts cited China’s control over critical rare-earth exports; Chinese rare-earth shipments to the United States remained about 75% below pre-restriction levels [8].
